```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 90)
# The evaluated examples run against a local replay of responses recorded from
# the production API: no network and no login at build time.
library(soilhub)
soil <- soilhub:::replay_session()
```

When you publish results obtained with soilhub (a thesis, a paper, a report, a
map), cite two things:

1. **the data**: the soil databases of ISRIC that you used. Their licences ask
   you to cite them;
2. **the tool**: the Global Soil Data Hub and the soilhub package, which
   gave you the data in that form.

## 1. Cite the data

Each dataset has its own citation. Read your data as usual; here, a few
WoSIS profiles around Vancouver:

```{r}
x <- soil_observations(soil, datasets = "wosis_points",
                       bbox = c(-123.3, 49.0, -122.9, 49.4),
                       max_rows = 5, progress = FALSE)
```

Then ask soilhub what to cite for the data in `x`:

```{r}
citations <- soil_citations(x)
writeLines(citations$citation_text)
```

The text is the one published by ISRIC, unchanged. Copy it into your list of
references. For WoSIS, ISRIC's text ends with an example download date:
write instead the date on which you read the data. If you read several datasets, `soil_citations()` returns one
citation for each of them.

For SOTER and SOTWIS, ISRIC gives no single citation for the whole dataset:
`soil_citations()` then returns the notes of each source database (country or
region), labelled as ISRIC labels them.

## 2. Respect the licences

Using the data is free, but under conditions set by the licence of each
source. `soil_licences()` gives the licence of the data you read:

```{r}
licences <- soil_licences(x)
writeLines(licences$licence_text)
```

In short, for the datasets of the hub (October 2026):

| Dataset | Licence | What it means for you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| WISE | CC BY 3.0 | free use, cite the source |
| SOTWIS | CC BY 3.0 | free use, cite the source |
| SOTER | CC BY 3.0 for 12 databases; CC BY-NC 3.0 for Malawi | cite the source; no commercial use of the Malawi data |
| WoSIS | a licence for each profile, chosen by the data provider | see below |

**WoSIS** collects profiles from many providers, and each profile keeps the
licence of its provider. Most profiles are public domain or CC BY (free use,
cite the source), but about a quarter of the WoSIS layers are CC BY-NC (**no
commercial use**) and a few are CC BY-SA (works derived from them must be
shared under the same licence). The hub keeps the licence of every profile;
showing it on each row of your data is planned for a next version of the hub.
Until then, if your use is commercial, check with ISRIC before using WoSIS
data.

What the licence names mean:

- **CC BY**: you may use, change and share the data, also commercially, if you
  cite the source;
- **CC BY-NC**: as CC BY, but **not for commercial purposes**;
- **CC BY-SA**: as CC BY, and what you derive from the data must be shared
  under the same licence;
- **CC0** and **public domain**: no conditions (citing the source is still good
  practice).

## 3. Cite the hub and the package

The data reach you through the **Global Soil Data Hub**, which keeps an exact
copy of the ISRIC databases, and through this package. Cite them as well,
especially if you used the revised view (`view = "revised"`): its rules are
part of the hub, not of the ISRIC data.

> Langella G. (2026). *soilhub: R client for the Global Soil Data Hub*
> (version 0.2.0) [software]. https://github.com/giulange/soilhub-r

A permanent identifier (DOI) will be added to this citation with the release
of version 0.2.0.

## 4. An example of a methods sentence

> Soil profile data (WoSIS; Batjes et al., see the citation returned by
> `soil_citations()`) were obtained from the Global Soil Data Hub with the R
> package soilhub (Langella, 2026), in the raw view (data as published by
> ISRIC).

Replace "raw view" with "revised view" if you used `view = "revised"`, and
list the rules that changed your data with `soil_revised_rules()`.

```{r teardown, include = FALSE}
soilhub:::replay_stop(soil)
```
